Moses is referring to the whole body by naming two major components, an arm and a head.
33:21: The phrase saw the first for himself was a common expression meaning to choose the best or first portion of the land.
The implication is that the portion of a commander refers to the best or largest share of land, appropriate for a leader.
Moses is speaking of the leaders of the people as if they were the heads of the people.

Moses is speaking of Naphtali’s abundant blessings as if favor and the blessing of the Lord were food or drink with which he could be satisfied and full.
Moses is speaking of the land around the Sea of Chinnereth (now known as “the Sea of Galilee”) by referring to its location as the west and the south.
33:24: The phrase Blessed among sons is Asher could mean: (1) a hope that Asher is more blessed than his brother (tribes); or (2) a hope that Asher’s sons bless the tribe more than the sons of other tribes.
Moses says bathe in oil his foot as an overstatement for emphasis.
33:25: Moses is speaking of the strength and security of Asher’s defenses as if the bolts of their gates were made of iron and bronze.

Moses is speaking of God as if he were riding the heavens and traveling on the clouds like a warrior riding a chariot to battle.
33:27: Moses is speaking of God as if he were a refuge or shelter.
Moses is speaking of God’s support as if he were holding his people up with eternal arms.

33:28: Here, spring of Jacob represents the descendants of Jacob, pictured as flowing from him like water from a spring.
Together, the terms grain and new wine represent God’s material blessings and provision for his people.
33:29: Moses is using the question form to emphasize that no other people are like Israel.
Here Moses is speaking of the Lord as if he were a shield that protects and helps Israel.
Moses is speaking of the Lord bringing Israel majesty and triumph as if he were a sword used in a victorious battle.
Here the author is speaking of completely defeating their enemies as if they would trample their enemies’ backs.
Moses is using fawn over you as a common expression of his culture to mean that their enemies would submit out of fear or feign obedience.

The word backs could mean: (1) the backs of the enemies, indicating that Israel will subjugate them. (2) the high places where the enemies worship, indicating that Israel will destroy their places of worship.
34:1: Here, against the face of represents being in front of or across from Jericho.
34:4: Here Moses is speaking as if the Israelites’ offspring were seed.
The Lord is using one part of a person, his eyes, to mean all of him in the act of seeing.
34:5: The author is using one part of the Lord, his mouth, to represent the Lord himself in the act of speaking or commanding.
34:6: The author assumes that readers will know that to this day refers to the time when this book was written, not to the time when Moses died.
34:7: The author is using a son of 120 years as a common expression of the culture to indicate Moses’s age.
The author is speaking of Moses’s eyesight as if his eye were something that could become dim.
The author is speaking of vigor as if it were a living thing that could flee.
34:9: The author is speaking of Joshua as if he were a container and the spirit of wisdom were a substance that could fill that container.
Moses’ laying his hands on Joshua was a symbolic action by which Moses showed that he was transferring authority to Joshua.
Here, sons means “descendants.” Moses is identifying the Israelites as descendants of their ancestor Jacob, who was also known as Israel.
Here the word listen means to intentionally hear and obey. See the discussion about this in the Introduction to Deuteronomy for further information.
34:10: The author is speaking of a prophet appearing or beginning to function as if he were arisen.
34:11: The terms signs and wonders mean similar things. The author is using the two terms together for emphasis.
34:12: Here the word hand represents God’s power.
Here, before the eyes represents sight or witnessing.
